`pack.py` now includes a held order only when its `approved` field is exactly `yes`. I reran it on `orders.csv`, and the report matches what I expected:

```
sku,units,cartons
birch_tea,7,2
cedar_mug,9,2
```

| Order | SKU | Units | Status / approved | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p1 | Cedar-Mug | 4 | ready / no | included |
| p2 | cedar_mug | 5 | ready / no | included |
| p3 | CEDAR MUG | 8 | hold / no | left out (not approved) |
| p4 | Birch-Tea | 2 | ready / no | included |
| p5 | birch_tea | 5 | hold / yes | **now included** |
| p6 | Birch Tea | 4 | cancelled / yes | left out (cancelled) |

- **birch_tea**: 2 + 5 = 7 units, so 2 six-unit cartons (it was 2 units in 1 carton).
- **cedar_mug**: unchanged at 9 units in 2 cartons. p3 is still left out, which shows the proposal to include every held order was not applied.

The code change is limited to the order filter in `pack.py`. SKU normalization and six-unit cartons are unchanged. I updated the assertion I run after each report to expect `birch_tea,7,2`, and it passed.

In the project memory, I replaced the old rule that all held orders stay out with the new exception. It also records that including every held order was rejected and that cancelled orders stay out even when approved.
